A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAVP research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original TAVP results on RLBench, component ablations, sensitivity and generalization experiments, and qualitative real-robot executions.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and adds quantitative real-world comparisons, robustness tests, and a demonstration-budget study.

M1.justification: The overview changes TaskMoE's stated placement from 'before MVT' to 'within the MVT'. The PDFs do not explain whether this reflects an architectural change or a corrected description. Expert routing, viewpoint prediction, losses, and three-stage training otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds real-world Collect Fruits and Put Item In Drawer evaluations and Pick Grape scenarios involving unseen instances, backgrounds, objects, heavy occlusion, and lighting variation. The 18 RLBench tasks remain unchanged. Older kettle-placement and lid-covering executions remain in appendix Figure 6, so those examples were not wholly removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds C2F-ARM-BC, PerAct, HiveFormer, PolarNet, RVT, Act3D, and 3D Diffuser Actor to the retained RVT2, ARP, and ARP+ comparisons. Diffusion Policy becomes a quantitative real-world comparator in Tables 4 and 7; the qualitative ARP+ comparison remains.

E3.justification: The reported real-world training budget changes from 100 to 50 demonstrations per task, and the three-D405 camera arrangement changes to D435i, D455, and wrist-mounted D405 cameras. New real-world evaluations specify ten trials per task or condition. Table 8 introduces 20/40/80/100-demonstration training budgets, and Table 2 adds a fixed-view control.

E4.justification: v2 adds a fixed-view ablation alongside the existing random-view ablation, tests five real-world distribution shifts, and examines performance across demonstration budgets. These address view-planning benefits, robustness, and data efficiency. Existing viewpoint-count, radial-range, latency, and zero-shot analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes from point estimates to mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for TAVP and several baselines, including the retained RVT2. Table 8 also reports mean ± standard deviation. Neither version specifies the corresponding run counts or seeds, so this establishes expanded uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises TAVP's reported average from 86.7% to 86.6%, with changes such as Place Cups 44% to 54% and Put in Safe 92% to 78%. v2 also adds comparator scores, an 83.33% fixed-view ablation, real-world averages of 88% versus Diffusion Policy's 68%, and robustness and data-efficiency results. The real-world additions use v2's revised setting.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical content. The added main-text statement that cameras face the origin restates the camera parameterization already present in v1 Appendix B. No new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and concluding discussion retain the same central claims about active viewpoint planning, TaskMoE, manipulation performance, and generalization. Naming TaskMoE explicitly in the abstract does not introduce a new contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new robustness results as improved adaptability and identifies heavy occlusion as a principal failure condition. It also attributes data-efficiency gains to architectural improvements. The latency and reflective/transparent-object limitations are moved from Appendix D into Section 5 without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Real-world documentation specifies right-arm use and revises camera models and placements, accompanied by an updated setup image. Core GPU specifications, model hyperparameters, preprocessing descriptions, and the appendix hyperparameter table remain unchanged. The code/project link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds distinct references for HiveFormer, Act3D, and PolarNet to support broader comparisons. Its additional 3D Diffuser Actor entry refers to work already cited in v1. The related-work narrative and positioning of TaskMoE and viewpoint planning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 introduces numbered sections, standardizes some MVEP terminology, removes a repetitive sampling explanation, moves real-world setup into the main text, and incorporates appendix limitations into the concluding section. Author affiliations and several local wording errors are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands Table 1, adds three result tables, and extends Table 2. Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer aggregation and position labels; the real-robot setup image is replaced and moved into the main text. The standalone real-world demonstration panel is removed, while execution sequences and other appendix figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical support for the paper's practical and view-planning claims. It supplements v1's qualitative real-world evidence with ten-trial baseline comparisons and stress tests, and adds a relevant fixed-view control beyond the random-view ablation. Broader comparisons and uncertainty reporting further improve assessment of the results. Run counts remain unspecified, and some commentary is unreconciled with updated results, notably the claimed Meat off Grill gains despite Table 1's lower score.
